eligibility_reason: Edges and gaps change flower production, fruit set and nectar robbing, but the source does not estimate pollinator and robber responses to flower production as one shared plant trait axis.
source_basis: Magrach, Santamaria & Larrinaga 2012 Austral Ecology DOI 10.1111/j.1442-9993.2011.02320.x
notes: Nectar robbing is up to sevenfold higher in gap-rich patches and lowers reproductive success; this is a habitat-context effect, not an H1 flower-production geometry.

eligibility_reason: Bird pollinators spend more time on white morphs, but this has no apparent fecundity consequence and realized fecundity is not directly associated with color; seed-predation selection is not directly on color.
notes: Color is retained as one-sided/null at the plant-fitness geometry ceiling despite a pollinator behavioral preference.

eligibility_reason: Flower number is positively correlated with nectar, seed-predator occurrence and long-term seed production, but the positive fecundity route is not isolated as pollinator-mediated selection on flower number.
notes: The trait is biologically important but does not license a pollinator-versus-seed-predator component geometry.

eligibility_reason: The congeners differ not only in flowering schedule but also floral morphology and breeding system, so species-level cost-benefit differences cannot be assigned to phenology alone.
notes: Retained as comparative ecological context, not a same-axis H1 trait geometry.

function_1: pollen limitation and selfing-mediated reproductive assurance
eligibility_reason: Small-flowered populations have less pollen limitation and less florivory, but selfing changes the reproductive route and florivores do not generally prefer large flowers within populations; the study itself concludes reduced florivory is likely a consequence of mating-system differentiation.
source_basis: Dart et al. 2015 Annals of Botany DOI 10.1093/aob/mcu242 plus associated Camissoniopsis dissertation/program
notes: Geographic covariation is strong, but it is not promoted to direct pollinator-versus-florivore selection on corolla width.

eligibility_reason: Chemotype significantly affects florivore visits, whereas the overall pollinator chemotype effect is weak/null and germination is affected by chemotype but not florivore visits.
source_basis: Sasidharan et al. 2024 Functional Ecology DOI 10.1111/1365-2435.14673
notes: Pollinator response to chemotype appears only marginal/context-specific in homogeneous plots, supporting one-sided/context-dependent geometry rather than conflict.

eligibility_reason: Heterogeneous plots receive more pollinator visits while florivore visits do not respond to plot type; germination correlates positively with pollinator visits but is not directly increased by plot type.
source_basis: Sasidharan et al. 2024 Functional Ecology DOI 10.1111/1365-2435.14673
notes: This is one-sided ecological geometry at the plot-diversity scale, not pollinator-florivore conflict.

eligibility_reason: Many-flowered plants are more central and receive more flower visits, but connectivity is driven mainly by antagonists and does not translate into higher reproductive success; pollinator species are effective but the flower-number benefit is not recovered as positive fitness selection in this network analysis.
notes: Same biological flower-number axis as SCHPRISMA-000312; this source adds a network context in which antagonist dominance yields one-sided/null realized geometry.
